UPSTREAM: mb/google/hatch: Change the DEVSLP reset config to PLTRST In S3 the PCH is driving the DEVSLP signal low, assuming that the SATA device is already powered off. However on hatch the SATA power is still enabled. And, since DEVSLP is low, this causes the SATA device to not enter low power state. The fix here is to set the pad config to be reset on PLTRST assertion which will cause the pin to be high impedance state and will be pulled up by the SATA device. BUG=b:126611255 BRANCH=None TEST=Make sure that S3 and S0ix is working fine on hatch. And also make sure that DEVSLP is pulled high in S3. Change-Id: I2ac43715ea52f626bb4aa5081a95262656de9a5e Signed-off-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@google.com> Original-Commit-Id: b866610156f88fdb0cbe96887d6ee84567aa521c Original-Change-Id: Ifb6a71a72244522c8dd8d48e9b9f8dc6feef8981 Original-Signed-off-by: Rizwan Qureshi <rizwan.qureshi@intel.com> Original-Reviewed-on: https://review.coreboot.org/c/coreboot/+/32136 Original-Tested-by: build bot (Jenkins) <no-reply@coreboot.org> Original-Reviewed-by: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1553857 Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Commit-Ready: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org> Tested-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org>

BACKPORT: FROMLIST: cros_ec: handle MKBP more events flag CL:1341159 adds a "more events" flag to allow the EC to notify us that there are more MKBP events waiting to be served. This CL extends the cros_ec bottom-half IRQ handler to listen to that flag in order to try and serve all known events before returning to the kernel with IRQ_HANDLED. This serves an optimization purpose as it minimizes the round-trip back and forth from the interrupt handler, and it also improves the quality of sensor timestamping, as it avoids a mismatch of event times between EC and AP that can confuse the median filter we use in the sensor ring. As described in the EC CL, this change is forward and backward compatible. This would be a cherry-pick of CL:1340983, but the code structure is different enough between kernel versions 4.4 and 4.14 that several tweaks are required to make things compile and work. It has been sent upstream as https://lore.kernel.org/patchwork/patch/1019477/ BUG=b:119570064, b:112102925, b:114915792 TEST=verify that sensor events come in and have sensible values and timestamps I had to tweak the merge of cros_ec_proto, but it was straight forward. FROMLIST: mfd: cros_ec: check for NULL transfer function As new transfer mechanisms are added to the EC codebase, they may not support v2 of the EC protocol. If the v3 initial handshake transfer fails, the kernel will try and call cmd_xfer as a fallback. If v2 is not supported, cmd_xfer will be NULL, and the code will end up causing a kernel panic. Add a check for NULL before calling the transfer function, along with a helpful comment explaining how one might end up in this situation. kernel: use compressed binary AFDO profiles when possible We recently switched Chrome to use compressed binary AFDO profiles, which saves us much CPU time and memory per TU. Kernel AFDO profiles are much smaller than Chrome's, so our per-TU savings is much smaller (around 50ms of CPU, and around 24MB of RAM). For full kernel builds with ccache disabled, `emerge-eve chromeos-kernel-4_4` uses 6% less CPU with this change. Peak memory usage is presumably dominated by linking, so it sees no change.
